exposure: Ureaplasma urealyticum (U. urealyticum) detection in neonatal urine
U. urealyticum detection in placental specimens
Dual-site detection of U. urealyticum (in both urine and placenta)
outcome: Adverse neonatal outcomes (sepsis, severe pneumonia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, brain injury, gastrointestinal bleeding/perforation, myocardial injury, death)
cohort: This retrospective cohort included 227 preterm neonates born between January 2020 and December 2022 at Jinan Maternal and Child Health Hospital.
finding: Combined detection of U. urealyticum in neonatal urine and placenta identifies preterm infants at the highest risk of adverse outcomes, suggesting a cumulative effect.
mod_finding: Urinary U. urealyticum positivity was associated with vaginal delivery.
gest_age: Preterm births; lower gestational age (<=28 weeks) mentioned in relation to findings.
